newsitem.title: USA: USDA SAYS 96/97 world wheat harvest second highest.
newsitem.headline: USDA SAYS 96/97 world wheat harvest second highest.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Tuesday said projected world wheat output in 1996/97 would be the second highest on record.
On Friday, USDA pegged 1996/97 world wheat production at 581 million tonnes, up from 579.5 million forecast in September and nearly 45 million tonnes higher than 1995/96.
Wheat harvests in Australia and the European Union were raised from last month's estimates, and the projected harvest from Canada was kept unchanged at a bumper level.
Big wheat importing nations, notably China and North African countries, were also projected to have bumper crops.

In its monthly Wheat Outlook, USDA's Economic Research Service noted world wheat trade projections for 1996/97 were raised in October to 90.8 million tonnes, up 2.2 million from September's estimate but the lowest since 1986/87.
It said trade was boosted due to higher projected imports by South Korea and Eastern Europe.
South Korea is now expected to substitute more feed wheat for corn as additional feed wheat supplies are anticipated in world markets, primarily from Canada.
